title: Cancellation at the Named Insured's Request and the Return Premium — HomeGuard Homeowners Policy
content:
## Conditions of cancellation

The named insured of a HomeGuard Homeowners Policy may cancel at any time. The request is recorded and must be signed by the named insured before it is processed.

- **Signed request.** The cancellation is processed only on a request the named insured has signed, as the recorded request shows.
- **No backdating.** The requested cancellation date is not earlier than the date the signed request is received. A request received on 12 May may ask for 12 May or any later date, never 11 May.
- **Date after expiration.** A requested date after the expiration date is not a cancellation; the policy is simply not renewed at the insured's direction.
- **Mortgagee.** The mortgagee, when on file, is notified of the cancellation.

## Package basis

The return basis follows the policy's package, each package carrying its own figures:

| Package figure | Role in the computation |
|---|---|
| Cancellation return basis (pro rata or short rate) | whether a retention is kept from the unearned premium |
| Short-rate retention percentage | the share of the pro-rata unearned premium kept on a short-rate cancellation |
| Minimum earned premium | the premium the carrier keeps at minimum for the term |

## Flat cancellation

When the requested date is on or before the effective date of a policy that is still bound, the cancellation is flat: the whole term premium is credited on a flat basis and no minimum earned premium applies.

## Midterm cancellation: the credit

1. **Current annual premium** — the term premium, together with the signed annual premium change of every endorsement of the term whose prorated premium was billed or credited (an increase adds, a decrease subtracts).
2. **Pro-rata unearned premium** — the current annual premium multiplied by the calendar days from the cancellation date to the expiration date, divided by the calendar days in the term, rounded half-up to the cent.
3. **Returnable amount** — on the pro rata basis, the whole unearned premium (credited as pro rata); on the short rate basis, the unearned premium less the package's short-rate retention percentage of it (credited as short rate).
4. **Cancellation credit** — the returnable amount less the term's scheduled installments not yet billed, because unbilled installments are simply never billed.
5. **Minimum earned premium** — the credit is then reduced, if needed, so that the premium kept for the term (everything billed for the term less the credit) is at least the package's minimum earned premium.
6. **Posting** — a positive credit is posted as one return premium entry dated the cancellation date, and any resulting credit balance is refunded under the HomeGuard refund rules. When the credit works out below 0.00, no credit is posted and the difference is billed as one additional premium entry with no credit basis, dated the cancellation date.

A carrier-initiated cancellation (nonpayment, uncured condition, material misrepresentation or substantial hazard increase) always credits pro rata, with no retention and no minimum earned premium.

## Worked figures (all inputs hypothetical)

Term of 365 days; term premium 1200.00; one endorsement of the term, annual change of 73.00 increase, prorated premium billed; cancellation date leaving 146 days to expiration.

- Current annual premium: 1200.00 and 73.00 together, 1273.00.
- Unearned: 1273.00 multiplied by 146, divided by 365, gives 509.20.
- Pro rata basis: returnable 509.20. Short rate basis with a 10 percent retention: 50.92 kept, returnable 458.28.
- One quarterly installment of 300.00 not yet billed: pro rata credit 509.20 less 300.00, which is 209.20.
- Billed for the term 900.00: kept 900.00 less 209.20, which is 690.80; with a minimum earned premium of 100.00 no reduction is needed. A return premium of 209.20 is posted.

Minimum earned premium biting (hypothetical): billed for the term 150.00, credit 120.00, minimum earned 100.00. Kept would be 30.00, below 100.00, so the credit is reduced to 50.00.

Credit below zero (hypothetical): returnable 100.00, unbilled installments 300.00. The credit works out at 200.00 below zero; no credit is posted and 200.00 is billed as additional premium dated the cancellation date.
